newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: AUDIOFINA SAYS MAY INVEST MORE IN CLT-UFA.
newsitem.headline: AUDIOFINA SAYS MAY INVEST MORE IN CLT-UFA.

text.p: Belgian-Luxembourg media holding company Audiofina said on Tuesday it might need to invest more in the expansion of its 49 percent owned unit CLT-UFA, Europe's largest television concern.

"CLT plans to invest several hundreds of millions of marks year after year... They will definitely need extra shareholder funds one day," Audiofina director Didier Bellens told a news conference on recently-formed CLT-Ufa.
The company is the product of a merger of Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) -- Audiofina's audiovisual unit -- with UFA, the television unit of German media group Bertelsmann .
Bellens said Audiofina in the future would use part of the 1.6 billion marks it will receive from Bertelsmann as part of the CLT-UFA merger deal for investments in CLT-UFA.
He expected CLT-UFA to have a profit margin of more than five percent of turnover. "The five percent mentioned would be on the low side. We have higher expectations than that."
"Once you are a number one in a market and you have a high percentage of audience share and of the advertising market, then these activities become very profitable," Bellens said.
